Codex banked resets now spend the credit that is about to expire and record what Codex actually answered, and devices and webhooks hear when a reset is used automatically, needs review or expires unused. Dashboard times use a 24-hour clock, and the proxy, usage storage and dashboard do less work per request.

## Changes

- **Codex banked resets.** Using a Codex reset names the credit that expires first, as OpenAI's own client does, so automatic use before expiry spends that credit rather than leaving the choice to Codex. Codex answers HTTP 200 whether or not it spent a credit, and Fusebox now reads its answer: `reset` is recorded as applied, `already_redeemed` as already used, `nothing_to_reset` and `no_credit` as refusals that keep the credit available, and anything else as an unknown outcome that blocks further spending until reviewed. Previously every 200 counted as applied. The confirmation dialog shows which credit will be used.
- **Banked-reset notifications.** A new **Banked resets** switch under Config → Notifications (`notifications.banked-resets`, on by default) sends push devices and webhooks a notice when automatic use spends a reset, when its outcome needs review, and when a reset expires unused, with the provider's last refusal if there was one. Each is sent once. Refusals on their own and resets you use yourself are not sent. A reset's expiry now triggers a fresh inventory read within about a minute.
- **24-hour times.** Dashboard dates and times use a 24-hour clock in the browser's time zone, whatever the browser's locale. Window-starter working hours are entered as HH:MM text instead of the browser's time picker, which showed AM/PM in some locales.
- **Lighter request path.** Wildcard model and policy matching no longer allocates, streamed SSE lines are borrowed from the received network chunk, and session inference no longer deep-copies image and other non-text blocks. Existing session hashes stay the same.
- **Usage storage and imports.** Health checkpoints skip unchanged writes. Detail reads, repricing, compaction and rollback reuse one bounded decoder per batch, with the same per-document checks. Plain history files resume from their checkpoint instead of rereading earlier bytes.
- **Dashboard and builds.** Hovering the usage chart and changing its grouping no longer rebuild the chart, and formatters and aggregates are reused. Asset builds reuse unchanged compressed output, and CI cancels superseded runs.

## Upgrading

- From v0.10.1, the usage database stays on schema 5; no database migration is introduced.
- Banked-reset notifications are on for configurations without the new setting. They go only to devices and webhooks you have already registered; set `banked-resets: false` under `notifications` to turn them off. Webhook consumers see a new `banked_reset` event, and a used reset has level `ok`.
- Expiry notices come from the running proxy: a reset that expires while Fusebox is stopped is not reported.

See [banked resets](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.11.0/docs/banked-resets.md), [notifications](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.11.0/docs/notifications.md) and the [optimization report](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.11.0/docs/efficiency-2026-10-29.md) for details.

[Full comparison with v0.10.1](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.10.1...v0.11.0).
